connection_profile_id.rationale: Identifies the connection profile but does not control authentication, authorization, encryption, network exposure, or data protection.

create_without_validation.description: Create the connection profile without validating it.
create_without_validation.rationale: Controls whether Datastream validates the connection before creation. It should be false so invalid credentials, unreachable endpoints, and incompatible connection settings are detected before the profile is accepted.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls protection against unintended profile deletion. PREVENT reduces the risk of accidental removal and disruption to dependent streams; DELETE or ABANDON permits removal from Terraform management.

display_name.rationale: Provides a human-readable name only and does not change the connection profile's security posture.

labels.description:
Labels.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Provides resource metadata for organisation and filtering but does not directly enforce access control, encryption, connectivity, or data protection.

location.description: The name of the location this connection profile is located in.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Selects the owning Google Cloud project but does not itself define IAM, encryption, network access, or another reusable security control; approved project identifiers are environment-specific.

forward_ssh_connectivity.hostname.rationale: Identifies the SSH tunnel endpoint. Its approved value is environment-specific, and the argument alone does not prove that the endpoint is trusted or securely configured.

forward_ssh_connectivity.password.rationale: Supplies team-specific SSH credential material. It does not configure a platform-level security control, and a reusable policy cannot determine whether the password is strong, rotated, or appropriately scoped.

forward_ssh_connectivity.port.rationale: Selects the SSH service port. A non-default port does not provide a meaningful security control, while an incorrect value primarily causes connectivity failure.

forward_ssh_connectivity.private_key.rationale: Supplies team-specific SSH credential material. Although key-based authentication may be preferred, the argument does not itself configure a reusable platform-level control or prove that the key is trusted and securely managed.

forward_ssh_connectivity.username.rationale: Identifies the SSH account but does not reveal whether that account has least privilege; approved usernames are environment-specific.

gcs_profile.bucket.rationale: Selects a team-specific destination bucket. It does not configure the bucket's platform-level IAM, encryption, retention, or public-access protections.

gcs_profile.root_path.description: The root path inside the Cloud Storage bucket.
gcs_profile.root_path.rationale: Selects a team-specific path within the destination bucket. It organises replicated data but does not create an access-control or encryption boundary.

mongodb_profile.description: Configuration for connecting to a MongoDB database.

mongodb_profile.password.description:
Password for the MongoDB connection. Mutually exclusive with
secretManagerStoredPassword.
mongodb_profile.password.rationale: Supplies team-specific MongoDB credential material. The platform-level control is the use of secret_manager_stored_password, rather than validating the password value itself.

mongodb_profile.replica_set.rationale: Selects the MongoDB replica set used for connectivity but does not independently enforce a security control.

mongodb_profile.secret_manager_stored_pa.description:
A reference to a Secret Manager resource name storing the MongoDB
connection password. Mutually exclusive with password.
mongodb_profile.secret_manager_stored_pa.rationale: References a Secret Manager secret instead of embedding the MongoDB password directly. Requiring a structurally valid secret version resource supports centralised secret storage, access control, auditing, and rotation.

mongodb_profile.username.rationale: Identifies the database account, but the value alone cannot establish that its database privileges follow least privilege.

mongodb_profile.host_addresses.description: List of host addresses for a MongoDB cluster.

mongodb_profile.host_addresses.hostname.rationale: Identifies a MongoDB endpoint. Approved hosts are environment-specific, and the value alone does not establish transport security or endpoint trust.

mongodb_profile.host_addresses.port.rationale: Selects the database service port. An incorrect value primarily affects connectivity and does not independently enforce a security control.

mongodb_profile.srv_connection_format.description:
Srv connection format. Mutually exclusive with
standard_connection_Format.

mongodb_profile.ssl_config.description: SSL configuration for the MongoDB connection.

mongodb_profile.ssl_config.ca_certificat.description:
PEM-encoded certificate of the CA that signed the source database
server's certificate.
mongodb_profile.ssl_config.ca_certificat.rationale: Supplies team-specific certificate material to the MongoDB TLS configuration. The certificate value itself is not a reusable platform-level setting because trust depends on the team's certificate authority.

mongodb_profile.ssl_config.client_certif.description:
PEM-encoded certificate that will be used by the replica to
authenticate against the source database server. If this field
is used then the 'clientKey' and the 'caCertificate' fields are
mandatory.
mongodb_profile.ssl_config.client_certif.rationale: Supplies team-specific MongoDB client certificate material. It does not independently configure a reusable platform-level control, and certificate trust and validity cannot be established from a generic value check

mongodb_profile.ssl_config.client_key.description:
PEM-encoded private key associated with the Client Certificate.
If this field is used then the 'client_certificate' and the
'ca_certificate' fields are mandatory.
mongodb_profile.ssl_config.client_key.rationale: Supplies team-specific MongoDB private-key material. The reusable platform-level control is storing the key through secret_manager_stored_client_key, not validating the key value itself.

mongodb_profile.ssl_config.secret_manage.description:
A reference to a Secret Manager resource name storing the
PEM-encoded private key. Mutually exclusive with clientKey.
mongodb_profile.ssl_config.secret_manage.rationale: References a Secret Manager secret for the MongoDB TLS client key. Requiring a structurally valid secret version resource reduces direct private-key exposure and supports controlled access and rotation.

mongodb_profile.standard_connection_form.description:
Standard connection format. Mutually exclusive with
srv_connection_format.

Specifies whether the client connects directly to the
host[:port] in the connection URI.
mongodb_profile.standard_connection_form.rationale: Chooses direct MongoDB topology behaviour and is deprecated; it primarily affects connection routing rather than enforcing authentication, encryption, or access control.

mysql_profile.hostname.rationale: Identifies the MySQL endpoint. Approved hosts are environment-specific, and the value alone does not establish transport security or endpoint trust.

mysql_profile.password.rationale: Supplies team-specific MySQL credential material. The platform-level control is the use of secret_manager_stored_password, rather than validating the password value itself.

mysql_profile.port.rationale: Selects the database service port. An incorrect value primarily affects connectivity and does not independently enforce a security control.

mysql_profile.secret_manager_stored_pass.description: A reference to a Secret Manager resource name storing the user's password.
mysql_profile.secret_manager_stored_pass.rationale: References a Secret Manager secret instead of embedding the MySQL password directly. Requiring a structurally valid secret version resource supports centralised secret storage, access control, auditing, and rotation.

mysql_profile.username.rationale: Identifies the database account, but the value alone cannot establish that its database privileges follow least privilege.

mysql_profile.ssl_config.description: SSL configuration for the MySQL connection.

mysql_profile.ssl_config.ca_certificate.description:
PEM-encoded certificate of the CA that signed the source database
server's certificate.
mysql_profile.ssl_config.ca_certificate.rationale: Supplies team-specific certificate material to the MySQL TLS configuration. The certificate value itself is not a reusable platform-level setting because trust depends on the team's certificate authority.

mysql_profile.ssl_config.client_certific.description:
PEM-encoded certificate that will be used by the replica to
authenticate against the source database server. If this field
is used then the 'clientKey' and the 'caCertificate' fields are
mandatory.
mysql_profile.ssl_config.client_certific.rationale: Supplies team-specific MySQL client certificate material. It does not independently configure a reusable platform-level control, and certificate trust and validity cannot be established from a generic value check.

mysql_profile.ssl_config.client_key.description:
PEM-encoded private key associated with the Client Certificate.
If this field is used then the 'client_certificate' and the
'ca_certificate' fields are mandatory.
mysql_profile.ssl_config.client_key.rationale: Supplies team-specific MySQL private-key material. It does not configure a reusable platform-level setting, and a generic policy cannot establish the key's ownership, strength, rotation, or protection.

oracle_profile.connection_attributes.rationale: Supplies database-specific connection parameters. Their meanings vary by environment, so this map does not provide a consistent, reusable security control by itself.

oracle_profile.database_service.rationale: Selects the Oracle database service but does not independently enforce authentication, encryption, or access control.

oracle_profile.hostname.rationale: Identifies the Oracle endpoint. Approved hosts are environment-specific, and the value alone does not establish transport security or endpoint trust.

oracle_profile.password.rationale: Supplies team-specific Oracle credential material. The platform-level control is the use of secret_manager_stored_password, rather than validating the password value itself.

oracle_profile.port.rationale: Selects the database service port. An incorrect value primarily affects connectivity and does not independently enforce a security control.

oracle_profile.secret_manager_stored_pas.description: A reference to a Secret Manager resource name storing the user's password.
oracle_profile.secret_manager_stored_pas.rationale: References a Secret Manager secret instead of embedding the Oracle password directly. Requiring a structurally valid secret version resource supports centralised secret storage, access control, auditing, and rotation.

oracle_profile.username.rationale: Identifies the database account, but the value alone cannot establish that its database privileges follow least privilege.

postgresql_profile.database.rationale: Selects the PostgreSQL database but does not independently enforce authentication, encryption, or access control.

postgresql_profile.hostname.rationale: Identifies the PostgreSQL endpoint. Approved hosts are environment-specific, and the value alone does not establish transport security or endpoint trust.

postgresql_profile.password.rationale: Supplies team-specific PostgreSQL credential material. The platform-level control is the use of secret_manager_stored_password, rather than validating the password value itself.

postgresql_profile.port.rationale: Selects the database service port. An incorrect value primarily affects connectivity and does not independently enforce a security control.

postgresql_profile.secret_manager_stored.description: A reference to a Secret Manager resource name storing the user's password.
postgresql_profile.secret_manager_stored.rationale: References a Secret Manager secret instead of embedding the PostgreSQL password directly. Requiring a structurally valid secret version resource supports centralised secret storage, access control, auditing, and rotation.

postgresql_profile.username.rationale: Identifies the database account, but the value alone cannot establish that its database privileges follow least privilege.

postgresql_profile.ssl_config.description: SSL configuration for the PostgreSQL connection.

postgresql_profile.ssl_config.server_and.description:
If this field is set, the communication will be encrypted with TLS encryption
and both the server identity and the client identity will be authenticated.

postgresql_profile.ssl_config.server_and.rationale: Supplies team-specific CA certificate material required by the selected PostgreSQL verification mode. The certificate value itself does not configure a reusable platform-level control.

postgresql_profile.ssl_config.server_and.description:
PEM-encoded certificate used by the source database to authenticate the
client identity (i.e., the Datastream's identity). This certificate is
signed by either a root certificate trusted by the server or one or more
intermediate certificates (which is stored with the leaf certificate) to
link to this certificate to the trusted root certificate.
postgresql_profile.ssl_config.server_and.rationale: Supplies team-specific PostgreSQL client certificate material required by the selected mutual-TLS mode. Its trust and validity cannot be established through a generic policy.

postgresql_profile.ssl_config.server_and.description:
PEM-encoded private key associated with the client certificate.
This value will be used during the SSL/TLS handshake, allowing
the PostgreSQL server to authenticate the client's identity,
i.e. identity of the stream.
postgresql_profile.ssl_config.server_and.rationale: Supplies team-specific PostgreSQL private-key material required by the selected mutual-TLS mode. It does not independently select or configure the platform-level verification mode.

postgresql_profile.ssl_config.server_ver.description:
If this field is set, the communication will be encrypted with TLS encryption
and the server identity will be authenticated.

postgresql_profile.ssl_config.server_ver.rationale: Supplies team-specific CA certificate material required by the selected PostgreSQL server-verification mode. The certificate value itself does not configure a reusable platform-level control.

private_connectivity.private_connection.description: A reference to a private connection resource. Format: 'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/privateConnections/{name}'
private_connectivity.private_connection.rationale: Supplies team-specific private connection material required by selected connectivity mode. The connection value itself does not configure a reusable platform-level control.

sql_server_profile.port.rationale: Selects the database service port. An incorrect value primarily affects connectivity and does not independently enforce a security control.
